newsitem.title: UK: New Euro wheat contracts face struggle - CFTC's Dial.
newsitem.headline: New Euro wheat contracts face struggle - CFTC's Dial.

text.p: Futures exchanges in Europe face an uphill struggle to spur demand for new agricultural contracts while risks are cushioned by subsidies, a top official of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) said on Monday.

But as government support diminishes, derivatives will see greater demand to transfer risk in more volatile markets, CFTC commissioner Joseph Dial said on the sidelines of a conference on Risk Management in Agriculture.
"All of these things have to unfold," he told Reuters. "Exchanges are head of the game and it takes time."

Amsterdam's Agricultural Futures Exchange (ARA) and the France's MATIF have seen scant interest for their newly-launched wheat futures and traders say the London International Financial Futures Exhange (LIFFE) will have similar problems unless it simply lists the world bechmark Chicago grain contracts for the European market.

MATIF's biggest headache is lack of participation by powerful grain cooperatives which fear that U.S. style hedging techniques may threaten the European Union's system of guaranteed prices and subsidies.
Dial said the relatively small size of the underlying cash market in Europe also appeared to be a problem.
